product.name: Hermes QA Dashboard
product.tagline: Unified QA automation, orchestration, and traceability powered by Hermes Agent.
product.repositoryDescription: Hermes Agent fork with a QA automation and traceability dashboard for versioned test assets, test plans, test cycles, execution monitoring, artifacts, reports, and Telegram delivery.
product.summary: Hermes QA Dashboard extends Hermes Agent with a structured workspace for managing QA configuration, reusable and versioned Test Assets, Test Plans, traceable Test Cycles, automated execution, evidence, results, reports, and delivery integrations.

foundation.dashboardFrontend: React 19, React Router, Zustand, and Vite
foundation.executionBackend: FastAPI and Hermes Agent QA execution services

personas.name: QA Engineer
personas.needs: Create reusable test definitions, prepare plans, execute cycles, review evidence, and track failures.

personas.name: QA Lead
personas.needs: Monitor test coverage, readiness, execution status, release quality, and historical trends.

personas.name: Developer
personas.needs: Understand failed tests, logs, evidence, affected features, and expected behavior.

personas.name: Technical Writer or Business Analyst
personas.needs: Maintain traceable requirements, test definitions, user flows, reports, and release documentation.

personas.name: Project Stakeholder
personas.needs: Review release status, risks, test coverage, and consolidated QA reports.

problemStatement: QA activities are often distributed across spreadsheets, chat messages, test scripts, screenshots, and independent execution tools. This makes test definitions difficult to reuse, historical results difficult to trust, and release status difficult to audit. Hermes QA Dashboard provides one traceable workflow from configuration and test design through execution, evidence, reporting, and delivery.
goals: Provide one unified Test Cycle for UI, API, Unit, E2E, and Related Regression testing.
Maintain reusable Test Assets with immutable version history.
Allow Test Plans and Test Cycles to preserve the exact Test Asset definitions used.
Connect Hermes Agent execution with structured monitoring, evidence, logs, and reports.
Provide reliable historical traceability from Project and Environment through Test Asset, Test Plan, Test Cycle, Execution, Result, and Artifact.
Deliver testing and documentation outputs to configured integrations such as Telegram.
Keep product documentation synchronized with dashboard development.
nonGoals: Providing a full enterprise identity and access management system during the MVP.
Providing production multi-tenant database persistence during the frontend MVP.
Executing every Test Asset definition individually before the execution mapping layer is implemented.
principles: Pages orchestrate data while feature modules contain business rules.
Presentational components do not access stores directly.
Test Plans and Test Cycles retain snapshot traceability.
Generated documentation must be reproducible and committed with the product.

modules.name: Dashboard
modules.description: Shows consolidated QA metrics, recent cycles, results, and operational status.

modules.name: Projects
modules.description: Manages product or application contexts used by Test Assets, Test Plans, and Test Cycles.

modules.name: Environments
modules.description: Manages target environments, URLs, and environment-to-project relationships.

modules.name: Test Assets
modules.description: Manages reusable UI, API, Unit, E2E, and Regression definitions with versioning and lifecycle controls.

modules.name: Test Planning
modules.description: Creates reusable Test Plans with scope, asset selection, execution settings, readiness, and captured asset versions.

modules.name: Test Cycles
modules.description: Creates and monitors unified testing cycles and scope executions.

modules.name: Test Cycle Asset Snapshots
modules.description: Preserves exact Test Asset versions through Test Cycle creation, execution request snapshots, historical detail, and version-aware reporting.

modules.name: History
modules.description: Provides historical execution and cycle records.

modules.name: Reports
modules.description: Provides consolidated QA results and immutable Test Asset version traceability with grouped Test Cycles, expandable asset details, shared filters, and cycle-level pagination.

modules.name: Integrations
modules.description: Manages Telegram and future delivery integrations, connection status, and resend controls.

modules.name: Documentation as Code
modules.description: Generates and validates PRD, architecture, user flows, user guidance, inventories, roadmap, and README content.

functionalRequirements.name: Project and Environment Management
functionalRequirements.description: Users can create and manage Projects and their target Environments.

functionalRequirements.name: Persistent Test Assets
functionalRequirements.description: Users can create reusable Test Assets for supported testing types.

functionalRequirements.name: Test Asset Versioning
functionalRequirements.description: Every Test Asset edit creates an immutable version with a mandatory change summary.

functionalRequirements.name: Test Asset Lifecycle
functionalRequirements.description: Test Assets can be archived and restored while preserving historical references.

functionalRequirements.name: Reusable Test Plans
functionalRequirements.description: Users can create reusable plans containing project, environment, scope, assets, and execution settings.

functionalRequirements.name: Test Plan Asset Snapshots
functionalRequirements.description: Test Plans capture immutable Test Asset versions and compare them with the live catalog.

functionalRequirements.name: Unified Test Cycle
functionalRequirements.description: Users can create cycles combining multiple testing scopes.

functionalRequirements.name: Test Cycle Asset Snapshots
functionalRequirements.description: Test Cycles preserve captured Test Asset definitions, compare them with the live catalog, and pass the immutable versions into execution request snapshots.

functionalRequirements.name: Execution Monitoring
functionalRequirements.description: Users can monitor execution status, telemetry, artifacts, results, and the immutable request snapshot used by each run.

functionalRequirements.name: Retry and Rerun Controls
functionalRequirements.description: Users can retry failed scopes, rerun selected assets, cancel execution, and duplicate cycles.

functionalRequirements.name: Traceable Reports
functionalRequirements.description: Reports include captured Test Asset versions, execution snapshot coverage, grouped Test Cycle traceability, expandable details, and pagination.

functionalRequirements.name: Telegram Delivery Management
functionalRequirements.description: Testing and documentation reports can be delivered, tracked, and resent through Telegram.

nonFunctionalRequirements.name: Traceability
nonFunctionalRequirements.description: Historical Test Plans, Test Cycles, and reports must not change when live Test Assets are modified.

nonFunctionalRequirements.name: Persistence
nonFunctionalRequirements.description: MVP frontend records persist locally and support versioned store migrations without losing user data.

nonFunctionalRequirements.name: Maintainability
nonFunctionalRequirements.description: Business rules remain in feature modules and presentational components remain independent from stores.

nonFunctionalRequirements.name: Documentation Integrity
nonFunctionalRequirements.description: Generated documentation must be reproducible and CI must detect stale generated files.

nonFunctionalRequirements.name: Security
nonFunctionalRequirements.description: Secrets and credentials must not be committed or rendered in documentation.

nonFunctionalRequirements.name: Compatibility
nonFunctionalRequirements.description: Existing Hermes Agent behavior and upstream attribution must remain preserved.

roadmap.name: Dashboard Foundation
roadmap.deliverables: React application, routing, layout, Project and Environment persistence.

roadmap.name: Test Asset Domain
roadmap.deliverables: CRUD, detail, versioning, lifecycle, linked usage, and immutable snapshots.

roadmap.name: Test Planning Domain
roadmap.deliverables: Plan catalog, detail, readiness, lifecycle, asset snapshots, and captured-versus-live comparison.

roadmap.name: Documentation as Code
roadmap.deliverables: PRD, architecture, user flows, user guide, generated inventories, README synchronization, and CI validation.

roadmap.name: Test Cycle Traceability
roadmap.deliverables: Cycle asset snapshots, captured-versus-live comparison, immutable execution request snapshots, and version-aware report traceability.

roadmap.name: Execution Controls
roadmap.deliverables: Retry failed, rerun scope, rerun asset, cancel, duplicate, and comparison controls.

roadmap.name: Reporting and Delivery
roadmap.deliverables: Version-aware reports, PDF or CSV export, Telegram delivery tracking, and resend controls.

roadmap.name: Production Persistence
roadmap.deliverables: Database persistence, authentication, authorization, audit trail, and concurrency control.

userFlows.name: Configure QA Context
steps: Create or select a Project.
Create or select an Environment for the Project.
Verify the target URL and execution context.

userFlows.name: Create a Versioned Test Asset
steps: Open Test Assets.
Create a Test Asset and define its type, module, feature, steps, and expected result.
Mark the asset as Execution Ready when its definition is complete.
Edit the asset with a Change Summary to create a new immutable version.

userFlows.name: Prepare a Test Plan
steps: Open Test Planning.
Choose Project, Environment, cycle type, and testing scope.
Select compatible Test Assets.
Configure execution and evidence settings.
Save the plan to capture current Test Asset versions.

userFlows.name: Create and Execute a Test Cycle
steps: Create a cycle directly or from a Test Plan.
Review Project, Environment, scope, and selected asset definitions.
Create the cycle and dispatch supported scope executions.
Monitor progress, telemetry, logs, results, and artifacts.
Review the consolidated result and release status.

userFlows.name: Review Historical Traceability
steps: Open a historical Test Plan or Test Cycle.
Review captured Test Asset version IDs and definitions.
Compare captured versions with the current live catalog.
Confirm each execution retained the cycle request snapshot.
Review version-aware report coverage and execution results.
